title: Predominant Th1/Th17 and Regulatory Response in Lung Tissues of Patients with Fatal Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
content: The analysis of the pulmonary microenvironment in six fatal cases of hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) provides valuable insights into the complex immunological and pathological mechanisms underlying disease severity. HPS is characterized by rapid respiratory deterioration, and understanding local immune responses within lung tissue is essential for elucidating why some infections progress to fatal outcomes. This study highlights several key factors, including cytokine production, immune cell activity, and alterations in pulmonary structure and function. Our findings suggest that excessive production of proinflammatory cytokines, particularly IL-6, together with a robust but dysregulated Th1 immune response, insufficient Treg-mediated immune regulation, and impaired surfactant function, may contribute to disease progression. These observations not only improve our understanding of HPS pathogenesis but also identify potential therapeutic targets, including cytokine modulation and strategies aimed at preserving pulmonary integrity, which may improve clinical outcomes in future patients.
